label: text
text: "Stoker Nagelin of the French cruiser "Jules Michelet" defenter "Kid". Alfred, the Filipino boxer on points in the main event on Saturday night at the Theatre Royal.

label: text
text: As usual the whole programm. was well up to the usual H.K.B.A standard. All the boats but one went the full distance.

label: paragraph_title
text: Featherweight.

label: text
text: In the third Choules made use of openings presented by his oponent. It was clean, open fighting.

label: text
text: Hallyway through the fourth Johnson was seen to have a quantity of blood on his face, and he had obviousy got a nasty cut above the eye. He was not allowed to continue and Choules received the decision.

label: paragraph_title
text: Welterweight

label: text
text: L. T. Emerson ("Tamar") was matched with L. S. Derbyshire ("Vindictive") and the first round was very quiet. Emerson led with his left but there was hardly an effective blow struck. Emerson was superior in the second and was obviously the fitter of the two.

label: text
text: In the third, Emerson was again ahead, Derbyshire lacking in defence. Derbyshire found the mark on a few occasions in the fourth, but his opponent's left kept hammering at him and he failed to defend himself against it. Emerson led in the fifth and sixth, and man out a worthy winner.

label: paragraph_title
text: 3untamweight.

label: text
text: 1. S. Hanson ("Vindictive") v. Pte. Baxter (East Surveys), Baxter proved to be quick on his feet and a hard hitter, but Hanson stood up to him calmly, and in the first there was not a great deal to choose between the two. In the second Baxter rattled his mum with several heavy blows to the jaw, but Hanson stuck up to him well.

label: text
text: Hanson improved wonderfully in the third, and administered severe punishment. He got in several niceshots to the jaw, and Baxter was badly marked when the gong went. Hanson came up very fresh for the fourth, and was slightly superior. Baxter was still fighting well in the fifth. In the last round, Hanson was better than his opponent, and received the decision, a fair one on points.

label: paragraph_title
text: Heavyweight

label: text
text: P. O. Francis (L. 3) met A. B. Moir ("Durban") at even weights in a ten round contest, and Francis, "with his advantage in height and reach was slightly superior. The second opened briskly, both men hitting hard but with little apparent effect. Moir's dashes did not benefit him to any great extent in the third, and his left was not a strong attacking point. text: Boxed coolly. Rush tincties prevailed in the next round, and in the succeeding one fighting was a little scrappy, with Moir bittling anywhere he could.

label: text
text: The sixth session saw some in-fighting, and when blows were exchanged Francis effectually blocked 'Moir's rushes'. The seventh was a mere repetition of exceeding rounds, featuringness in the most part. Moir was cautioned in the eighth and eventually received the decision in an unpatis factory fight.

label: text
text: Nagelin weighed in a 120½ lbs. and Alfred 118½.

label: text
text: First Round:—Alfred hit hard but Nagelin won the round and scored a well-timed blow to the jaw as the gong went.

label: text
text: Second Round: Good clean farthing, with some smart footwork. Alfred was a little canless, but he fought well.

label: text
text: Third Round: Nagelin punished Alfred on the ropes, but the Filipino swung the Frenchman round with a hard blow towards the end. Fast and interesting.

label: text
text: Fourth Round: -Nagelin led with his left, and jaured, the Filipino once or twice. Alfred did not seem to use his right to the best advantage.

label: text
text: Fifth Round: The Frenchman got in a left hook to the chin. Alfred replying with an equally active night cut.

label: text
text: Sixth: Roundtall—Alfred used swings with effect, but the French-mun's left was always dangerous. Not much to choose between the two.

label: text
text: Seventh Round:—In favour of the Frenchman. He punished the Kid rather sensibly, and was eiever in dodging on the ropes.

label: text
text: Eighth Round: Alfred's. He attacked from the start and certainly pulled up a little on points. The Frenchman was very cool, however, and fought back well.

label: text
text: Ninth Round: — Alfred's round again. He had got the measure of his opponent, and used his left to advantage. Both sticking the race well. Now about even on points.

label: text
text: Tenth Round—Perhaps Nagell find a slight advantage here. Alfred showed up better at in-fighting but the pace, compared with that of the ninth, dropped off considerably.

label: text
text: Eleventh Round: Nagelin once got through his opponent's defence and gave him a good deal of punishment. It was an excellent fight up to this point, being keenly contested.

label: text
text: Twelfth Round: — Alfred blocked Nagelin's blows effectively, but Nagelin made openings and led on points at this stage. The Kid failed to maintain the improvement shown in the eighth and ninth rounds.

label: text
text: Thirteenth Round: — Nagelin's round. He proved himself a capable and very clever fighter. The Filipino was by no means overshadowed however. He was fighting well.

label: text
text: Fourteenth Round:—Alfred striving for a knock-out. It was his only chance of winning, and he tried hard to make an opening. Many of his blows missed.

label: text
text: Fifteenth Round:—A hard round to finish a splendid fight. Both men fought well, but the Filipino could not get in a knock-out blow. Nagelin got the verdict—a popular one, and one he thoroughly deserved.

label: text
text: The remaining contest was between Stoker Reynolds (L.3) and Private Mann (East Surreys) and it proved to be a clean open fight with Reynolds superior in the first and second. He administered severe punishment. Both boxed in good style and a fast pace was maintained. Hit and counter-hit was the rule, and up to the end of the fourth there was not a great deal to choose between the two. In the next two rounds, as in the previous ones, both men fought splendidly in a fight which was characterised by an almost total absence of in-fighting. It was thoroughly enjoyable-contest, clean and full of interest. Reynolds ran out winner.
